newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour wants to replace Camelot.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour wants to replace Camelot.

text.p: The opposition Labour Party on Monday said it would like to replace Camelot Group Plc as the runner of Britain's National Lottery with a non-profit organisation.
But National Heritage spokesman Jack Cunningham said the replacement at the end of Camelot's current seven-year contract would ultimately be a matter for the OFLOT regulator.
And that would depend on an organisation coming forward which could manage the lottery competitively and efficiently, he told BBC radio.
Cunningham was speaking ahead of a Labour news conference to announce the party's policy on the lottery.
At the news conference, he said lottery money should be used for one-off projects such as training teachers to use new technology, insulating homes for the elderly and creating pedestrian-only zones.
Cadbury Schweppes Plc, De La Rue, Racal Electronics and GTECH Holdings each own a 22.5 percent stake in Camelot and Fujitsu Ltd has a 10 percent stake. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
